description: The bytes/platform half of ADR-0031 decision 2's N3-start corpus extension, asserted against `gatebraid/coverage-report@1` (admitted at N1E per ADR-0030's route). Covers the three blocked remainders DETERMINACY-REPORT.md §2 names for the BP items: BP-01's `sha256` re-derivation, BP-02's `byte_length` mismatch, and BP-03's cross-document dual-platform claim — the last of which §2 recorded as having 'nothing to mutate' because no committed artifact made a dual-platform claim. The coverage report is that artifact, which is why these items freeze here and not at N1. Every invalid case is a SINGLE mutation of a valid sibling: BP1-01 for most, BP1-02 for BP1-05 and BP1-06. Every locus was MEASURED, never written by hand. DIGESTS: `target.sha256` is the REAL SHA-256 of the committed file it names and re-derives; every other digest here is SYNTHETIC and is declared so, because the validator these reports describe does not exist yet — which is precisely what ADR-0031 defers. An internally incoherent fixture would be a bad fixture regardless of what the schema can see, so nothing is claimed as real that is not.

case_provenance: R3-D method, recorded because the difference is the point. Every case here was constructed by the N1E executor — which authored neither N2 nor N3 — from the ITEM'S WRITTEN DESCRIPTION in M3-PLAN.md §6, CORPUS-v1-PLAN.md §3 and DETERMINACY-REPORT.md §2, NOT from the N3 draft's candidate cases, which were not read until after these were measured. That is what supplies the not-authored-by-the-implementer property here, in place of an external contribution. The two constructions were then compared and BOTH were kept wherever they differed: BP1-03/BP1-04 (this executor) and BP1-08 (the N3 draft) are three distinct loci over the same two remainders, and neither construction found the other's; IN1-07 (this executor) and IN1-11 (the N3 draft) likewise; IN1-12 was reached only by the N3 draft. Cases marked `independently_constructed` were reached by this executor before N3's were read; those marked `n3_draft_contributed` were not, and are carried on the transcribe-then-re-measure method that worked for the seven externally contributed cases at N1D. The residual is named: these are NOT externally contributed, and no external party reviewed them.
known_limitation: MEASURED, by a sweep of every expected-locus set across all five corpora: NO collision involves any case in this corpus. Two relations remain UNENFORCEABLE here and are named rather than left looking enforced. (1) Whether `replay.rederived_sha256` EQUALS the digest the target claims is the arithmetic half of BP-01 and BP-02; it relates two documents and no JSON Schema keyword compares them. What is enforced is that a `replayed` claim cannot be made without a re-derived digest beside it (BP1-08), that the digest cannot be absent from a replay block (BP1-03), and that it must be digest-shaped (BP1-04). The comparison itself is N3's runtime duty. (2) An entry in `dual_platform_claim.reports` cannot be checked against the enclosing report's own digest, so a report citing ITSELF as one of its two platforms validates here; `uniqueItems` catches the same sibling cited twice (BP1-06) but not self-citation. Both are recorded as N3 re-derivation duties.
